The Straits are open to the Allies, the army is to go home and the garrisons in Arabia, Syria and Mesopotamia are to surrender. The war that the empire entered at the order of one minister and one German admiral ends with the empire's capital under Allied guns, and with a population that was told, for four years, that it was winning.-5MANPOWER ▾-7MUNITIONS ▾-5IMPERIAL CONTROL ▾Settled recordThe German ships, August 1914: kept out of the Straits. Entering the war, 1914: the fleet kept in the Bosphorus. Sarikamis, December 1914: the Erzurum line held through the winter. The Suez Canal, February 1915: the Fourth Army kept in Palestine. Gallipoli, April 1915: the divisions placed above the beaches. Kut, winter of 1915-16: the siege broken by the relief force. Erzurum, 1916: the fortress held until it fell. The Hejaz, 1916: Medina held to the end of the war. The Yildirim, 1917: sent to Palestine. Jerusalem, 1917: the city defended. The Caucasus, 1918: the Army of Islam sent to Baku.
